data_sources.description: Per-device last-seen timestamp compared against an expected reporting interval.

detection_logic: Computes the time since the last event from each known device and flags any exceeding the expected reporting interval.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen by host
| eval hours_since=round((now()-last_seen)/3600,1)
| where hours_since>24
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained inventory of expected-reporting devices to distinguish genuine silence from a decommissioned device — join against an asset inventory lookup in production.
investigation_steps: Check network reachability to the device's OOB IP directly.
If reachable but silent, treat as a likely logging-tamper incident.
response_guidance: Investigate immediately; a reachable-but-silent device is a strong anti-forensics indicator.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: no audit event received for >24 hours

title: iDRAC System Event Log (SEL) Cleared
description: The System Event Log — the hardware-level event history covering power state changes, thermal/voltage events, and (in many configurations) some security-relevant events — is cleared. Named explicitly by the specification alongside syslog redirection and log-service clearing as a top-priority anti-forensics indicator.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log
data_sources.path: LC log, category=Audit; also visible via Redfish LogServices

detection_logic: Filters the iDRAC audit log for SEL clear events. As with the syslog-disable case, ensure this event itself is captured by external forwarding before the clear takes effect.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit event="SELCleared"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during a documented maintenance procedure (e.g. after resolving a known hardware fault) — require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Preserve any externally-forwarded copy of the SEL before this event's window ages out.
Treat the clearing session as highly suspect.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed anti-forensics incident pending explicit authorization evidence.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iDRAC Repeated Chassis Intrusion Events
description: The chassis intrusion sensor records multiple open/close events within a short window. Individually a single legitimate service event, but repeated intrusion events outside a maintenance window are worth correlating against physical access logs where available.

data_sources.name: iDRAC SEL
data_sources.path: System Event Log, chassis intrusion sensor

detection_logic: Counts chassis-intrusion sensor events per device in a rolling window, cross-referenced against a maintenance-window lookup.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_sel event="ChassisIntrusion"
| lookup idrac_maintenance_windows.csv host _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count by host, _time
| where count>=2
tuning_guidance: Correlate with physical access/badge logs where available (outside this catalogue's scope) for higher confidence.
investigation_steps: Confirm against maintenance/service records.
Cross-reference with any hardware inventory change (LC-005).
response_guidance: Investigate physically if unaccounted for.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Same T1200 (Hardware Additions) closest-fit rationale as IDRAC-030, applied here to physical chassis-intrusion sensor events that may correlate with unauthorized hardware tampering.

title: iDRAC Unexpected Storage or NIC Hardware Removal
description: The SEL records a drive or NIC disappearing from the system outside a declared maintenance window — could reflect a genuine hardware failure, or physical component theft/tampering.

data_sources.name: iDRAC SEL
data_sources.path: System Event Log, component removal events

detection_logic: Filters the SEL for component-removal events outside a maintenance window.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_sel event="ComponentRemoved" component IN ("PhysicalDisk","NIC")
| lookup idrac_maintenance_windows.csv host _time OUTPUT in_window
| where isnull(in_window)
| table _time, host, component
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference with LC-005's inventory-change detection and any concurrent storage destruction detections (IDRAC-081).
investigation_steps: Confirm against maintenance records.
Investigate physical security if unaccounted for.
response_guidance: Investigate as potential physical tampering or theft if unaccounted for.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iDRAC TPM Failure or Firmware Integrity Failure in SEL
description: The SEL records a TPM failure or a firmware/BIOS integrity-check failure — the hardware-event-log corroboration of the IDRAC-041/IDRAC-051 configuration-side detections, useful when the tampering itself happens through a path that doesn't generate a configuration-change event (e.g. a genuine hardware fault vs. deliberate tampering can sometimes only be distinguished by examining the specific SEL sensor and event data).

data_sources.name: iDRAC SEL
data_sources.path: System Event Log, TPM/firmware integrity sensors

detection_logic: Filters the SEL for TPM and firmware-integrity sensor events.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_sel sensor IN ("TPM","Firmware Integrity")
| table _time, host, sensor, event_data
tuning_guidance: Distinguish a genuine hardware fault (consistent, reproducible failure) from a security event (correlated with other suspicious activity) by reviewing the full event_data field and surrounding timeline.
investigation_steps: Cross-reference with IDRAC-041/IDRAC-051 for a corresponding configuration-side event.
If no configuration correlate exists, treat as a probable genuine hardware fault pending vendor diagnostics.
response_guidance: Escalate to security if correlated with other suspicious activity; otherwise route to hardware support.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iDRAC RAID/Virtual Disk Deleted
description: A virtual disk (RAID logical volume) is deleted via iDRAC/PERC configuration. This destroys the storage array's data structure — an attacker with iDRAC access can destroy data at the storage-controller level entirely independent of, and unstoppable by, anything running in the host OS.
detection_logic: Filters the iDRAC audit log for virtual disk deletion events.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_storage event="VirtualDiskDeleted"
| table _time, host, user, controller, virtual_disk
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate case outside a fully-documented storage reconfiguration/decommissioning procedure.
investigation_steps: Confirm against change management immediately.
Assess data-loss impact — this action is not reversible without a backup.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed destructive incident if unaccounted for; engage backup/recovery procedures immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1561.002: Disk Structure Wipe

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iDRAC Disk Secure Erase or Foreign Configuration Import
description: A secure-erase operation is initiated on a physical or virtual disk, or a foreign RAID configuration (from a disk moved from another controller/server) is imported. Secure erase is irreversibly destructive; foreign-configuration import can be used to introduce disks with pre-existing (potentially malicious or exfiltrated) data into the array.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log
data_sources.description: Secure erase and foreign configuration import events.

detection_logic: Filters the iDRAC audit log for secure-erase and foreign-configuration-import events.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_storage event IN ("SecureErase","ForeignConfigImport")
| table _time, host, user, controller, event
tuning_guidance: Legitimate for a documented drive-decommissioning (secure erase) or drive-replacement (foreign config import) procedure — require a change ticket for either.
investigation_steps: For secure erase, confirm this data was intended for destruction.
For foreign config import, verify the origin of the imported disks.
response_guidance: Treat unaccounted-for secure erase as a confirmed destructive incident; investigate unaccounted-for foreign imports for data provenance.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1561.001: Disk Content Wipe

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iDRAC Storage Controller Reset
description: The RAID/PERC controller is reset. Can disrupt in-flight I/O and, depending on timing and array state, contribute to data integrity issues — tracked as a disruptive action in its own right, distinct from outright deletion.
detection_logic: Filters the iDRAC audit log for storage controller reset events.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_storage event="ControllerReset"
| table _time, host, user, controller
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during troubleshooting; require a change ticket outside a maintenance window.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Investigate if unaccounted for.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass Virtual Disk State Change Across Storage Fleet
description: Virtual disks go offline, are deleted, or are secure-erased across an unusually large number of distinct devices within a short window — the storage-destruction equivalent of IDRAC-036's mass power-action detection, and one of the clearest possible signals of a fleet-wide, maximally destructive management-plane compromise (e.g. a ransomware-adjacent extortion scenario targeting storage directly rather than encrypting data at the OS level).

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: LC log, category=Storage, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Storage-destructive events across the managed fleet.

detection_logic: Counts distinct devices with a storage-destructive event per acting user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_storage event IN ("VirtualDiskDeleted","SecureErase")
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices, values(host) as devices by user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=3
tuning_guidance: No legitimate steady-state pattern for this at fleet scale outside a fully-documented mass-decommissioning event.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live, maximally-critical incident.
Identify every affected device immediately.
response_guidance: Suspend the acting account/source immediately; this is a full-scale data-destruction incident requiring immediate executive and legal notification alongside technical response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1561.002: Disk Structure Wipe

author: Threat Detection Library

title: iDRAC Factory Reset
description: iDRAC is reset to factory defaults, wiping its entire configuration — accounts, network settings, logging destinations, certificates — in a single action. On a production server this is either a catastrophic operational mistake or deliberate sabotage/anti-forensics, and either way it destroys the very audit trail needed to investigate it.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log
data_sources.path: LC log, category=Audit (captured only if forwarded externally before reset completes)

detection_logic: Filters the iDRAC audit log for factory reset events; relies on external syslog forwarding to survive the reset itself.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit event="FactoryReset"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: No tuning — this should never occur on a production device outside a fully-documented decommissioning process.
investigation_steps: Confirm against decommissioning records immediately.
Preserve any externally-forwarded logs before they age out.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed incident if unaccounted for; this requires full investigation of how reset-level access was obtained.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: iDRAC Account Database or Lifecycle Controller Reset
description: The iDRAC user/account database is reset independently of a full factory reset, or the Lifecycle Controller itself is reset. Either removes existing account governance or job history without wiping every other configuration domain — a more targeted alternative to a full factory reset that can still achieve account-takeover or evidence-destruction goals.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log
data_sources.description: Account database / Lifecycle Controller reset events.

detection_logic: Filters the iDRAC audit log for account-database or Lifecycle Controller reset events.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit event IN ("AccountDatabaseReset","LCReset")
| table _time, host, user, event
tuning_guidance: No routine legitimate case outside a documented recovery procedure.
investigation_steps: Confirm against change/incident records.
Audit the resulting account roster against the expected baseline.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed incident if unaccounted for; rebuild the account roster from a known-good baseline.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1531: Account Access Removal

author: Threat Detection Library

title: OpenManage Enterprise Administrator Login Failure / Brute Force
description: Repeated failed administrator login attempts against Dell OpenManage Enterprise, the fleet management console that can discover, onboard, and push configuration/firmware to every iDRAC it manages — the Dell equivalent of FortiManager's blast radius in the Fortinet catalogue.
detection_logic: Counts failed OME admin logins in a rolling window.
spl:
index=ome sourcetype=ome_audit event="Login" result="Failed"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count, values(src_ip) as source_ips by user, _time
| where count>=5
tuning_guidance: Minimal legitimate tuning expected given OME's typically small administrator population.
investigation_steps: Validate targeted usernames.
Check for a subsequent success.
response_guidance: Block the source; treat with the same urgency as any Tier-0 management-plane authentication attack in this catalogue.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: OpenManage Enterprise Discovery/Credential Profile Changed
description: A discovery credential profile (the stored iDRAC/RACADM credentials OME uses to manage devices at scale) is modified. OME's discovery profiles are effectively a centralized store of credentials valid across the entire managed fleet — compromising this configuration is functionally equivalent to compromising every device it can reach.
detection_logic: Filters the OME audit log for discovery credential profile changes.
spl:
index=ome sourcetype=ome_audit event="CredentialProfileChanged"
| table _time, user, profile_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during planned credential rotation; require a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Verify the change against change management.
Assess whether the fleet-wide credential may now be compromised.
response_guidance: Rotate fleet-wide credentials immediately if the change is unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: OpenManage Enterprise Mass Firmware Baseline Deployment
description: A firmware baseline (potentially including a downgrade) is applied to an unusually large number of devices in a single OME job — the OME-driven equivalent of IDRAC-050's single-device firmware-downgrade detection, at fleet scale.

data_sources.name: OME audit log
data_sources.description: Firmware baseline deployment job events with target device count.

detection_logic: Filters OME firmware deployment jobs where the target device count exceeds a fleet-wide threshold.
spl:
index=ome sourcetype=ome_job event="FirmwareDeployment"
| where device_count>=10
| table _time, user, baseline_name, device_count
tuning_guidance: Baseline your organization's normal deployment scope for scheduled patch cycles; focus alerting specifically on downgrade baselines.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket.
Verify the baseline version is a forward (not backward) change.
response_guidance: Halt the deployment and roll back if it represents an unauthorized fleet-wide downgrade.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

title: OpenManage Enterprise Remote Command (RACADM/Script) Job
description: OME executes a remote RACADM command or custom script job against multiple devices — the Dell equivalent of the FortiManager script-execution detection (FMG-018). Since OME jobs run with the discovery profile's stored credentials against every targeted device, this is a powerful and easily fleet-scaled execution mechanism.

data_sources.name: OME audit log
data_sources.description: Remote command/script job events with target device count.

detection_logic: Filters OME job execution events for remote-command/script job types with a target device count above threshold.
spl:
index=ome sourcetype=ome_job event="JobExecuted" job_type IN ("RACADM","Script")
| where device_count>=5
| table _time, user, job_type, device_count
tuning_guidance: Baseline your organization's normal script-execution scope; allowlist known recurring maintenance script names.
investigation_steps: Immediately review the executed command/script content.
Identify every affected device.
response_guidance: Treat as a live incident if unauthorized: audit every affected device for the exact commands executed.

title: Same Administrator Accessing Unusually Many iDRACs
description: A single administrator account authenticates to an unusually large number of distinct iDRAC devices within a short window — could reflect legitimate fleet-wide maintenance, or a compromised credential being used to systematically access every device it's valid on.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: LC log, category=Audit, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Login events across the managed fleet.

detection_logic: Counts distinct devices accessed per user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit event="Login" result="Success"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices by user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=15
tuning_guidance: Baseline your organization's normal per-administrator device-access scope; allowlist known bulk-maintenance operators.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket for planned fleet-wide maintenance.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed, particularly in combination with any of the higher-severity actions in this catalogue.

title: Mass Secure Boot or TPM Change Across Fleet
description: Secure Boot is disabled or TPM state is changed across multiple distinct devices within a short window — the fleet-wide escalation of IDRAC-040/IDRAC-041, and one of the clearest signals of a boot-security-stripping campaign carried out via OpenManage Enterprise or a compromised shared credential rather than one device at a time.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: LC log, category=Configuration, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Secure Boot / TPM configuration changes across the managed fleet.

detection_logic: Counts distinct devices with a Secure Boot or TPM configuration change per acting user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit event="ConfigChange" cfgattr IN ("SecureBoot","TpmSecurity","TpmClear")
| bin _time span=30m
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices, values(host) as devices by user, cfgattr, _time
| where distinct_devices>=3
tuning_guidance: No legitimate steady-state pattern for this at fleet scale outside a fully-documented, rare compatibility migration.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live fleet-wide incident.
Identify every affected device and restore Secure Boot/TPM state immediately.
response_guidance: Suspend the acting account/source; restore boot-security settings fleet-wide and audit for any virtual-media or boot-override activity that may follow.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Same T1542 (Pre-OS Boot) closest-fit rationale as IDRAC-037/040, applied at fleet scale.

title: Mass Log Clearing or Syslog Redirection Across Fleet
description: SEL clearing, log-service clearing, or syslog-forwarding changes occur across multiple distinct devices within a short window — the fleet-wide anti-forensics escalation combining IDRAC-066, IDRAC-070, and REDFISH-006 across many devices at once, the clearest possible signal of a coordinated attempt to blind the organization's out-of-band management visibility ahead of a larger operation.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: LC log, category=Configuration/Audit, aggregated across devices
data_sources.description: Log-tampering events across the managed fleet.

detection_logic: Counts distinct devices with a log-clearing or syslog-redirection event per acting user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit (event="SELCleared" OR (event="ConfigChange" AND cfgattr IN ("SyslogEnable","SyslogServer")))
| bin _time span=30m
| stats dc(host) as distinct_devices, values(host) as devices by user, _time
| where distinct_devices>=3
tuning_guidance: No legitimate steady-state pattern at fleet scale.
investigation_steps: Treat as the highest-priority incident this catalogue can raise for iDRAC.
Preserve any remaining external logs immediately.

title: iDRAC Compromise Reaches OS-Level Boot Bypass via Virtual Media
description: The single most important attack chain in this catalogue, presented as a named, multi-stage correlation for reporting/dashboard purposes on top of the individual detections that compose it: an iDRAC administrator compromise (IDRAC-004), followed by virtual media mount (IDRAC-030/031), a one-time boot override to that media (IDRAC-032), and a reboot — the complete out-of-band OS-bypass sequence. Because iDRAC operates independently of the host OS, none of this activity would appear in any OS-level security tooling until the host boots into attacker-controlled media.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log (full session)
data_sources.description: Full timeline from authentication compromise through virtual media boot.

detection_logic: A four-stage transaction spanning login-after-failures, virtual media attach, boot override to media, and reboot, for the same device within a 30-minute window — the same underlying logic as IDRAC-032, extended to explicitly require the authentication-compromise precursor.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit
| eval stage=case(event="Login" AND result="Failed","0_auth_attempt", event="Login" AND result="Success","1_auth_success", event="VirtualMediaAttached","2_media_mounted", event="BootOverride","3_boot_override", event="PowerControl" AND action IN ("Reset","PowerCycle"),"4_reboot", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=45m startswith=eval(stage="0_auth_attempt")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=4
| table _time, host, user, src_ip, stage
tuning_guidance: This is a reporting/dashboard rollup of IDRAC-002/004/030/032 — implement each underlying detection first and treat this as a derived incident-timeline view.
investigation_steps: Pull the full timeline from initial authentication through reboot for the incident report.
Do not assume the host OS is trustworthy — full forensic imaging or rebuild may be required.
response_guidance: Power off the device, detach media, and treat the host OS as compromised pending full investigation; this is the highest-priority response scenario in the iDRAC catalogue.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: auth compromise -> virtual media mount -> boot override -> reboot

attack_mapping_note: Same T1200/T1542 closest-fit rationale as IDRAC-030/037 — the OS-level outcome of this chain is a bootloader/OS state that no longer matches what was originally installed, achieved via out-of-band media injection rather than any technique ATT&CK models natively for remote/virtual media.

title: iDRAC Firmware Downgrade Correlated With Fleet Configuration Import
description: A firmware downgrade (IDRAC-050) and a Server Configuration Profile import (LC-003) occur on the same device in close succession, or a mass Secure Boot/TPM change (IDRAC-111) coincides with an OME firmware baseline deployment (IDRAC-102) — combining two independently Critical findings into a single higher-confidence incident, on the theory that a downgrade paired with a configuration overwrite is far more likely to represent deliberate, coordinated tampering than either alone.

data_sources.name: iDRAC + OME logs
data_sources.description: Firmware and configuration-integrity events correlated by device and time.

detection_logic: Correlates a firmware-downgrade event with a subsequent (or preceding) Server Configuration Profile import for the same device within 2 hours.
spl:
index=idrac
| eval stage=case(sourcetype="idrac_lc" AND event="FirmwareUpdate" AND is_downgrade=1,"1_firmware_downgrade", sourcetype="idrac_lc" AND event="SCPImport","2_config_import", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=2h
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Legitimate during a coordinated, documented hardware refresh/migration — require a change ticket covering both actions together.
investigation_steps: Reconstruct the full timeline of both events.
Verify Secure Boot, TPM, and account roster state after both actions complete.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed coordinated tampering incident if unconfirmed; restore firmware and configuration from known-good baselines.

MITRE ATT&CK T1601: Modify System Image

author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: firmware downgrade + configuration profile import, same device

title: Privileged Identity Compromise Followed by iDRAC Access
description: A privileged directory-account compromise indicator from an external identity source (e.g. a SIEM-correlated Active Directory privileged-group change, or a FortiAuthenticator/IPA-equivalent identity event in an environment running one of this library's other catalogues) is followed by an iDRAC login for that same identity — the Dell-infrastructure analogue of the Red Hat catalogue's RH-X-001 (IPA identity compromise reaching RHEL SSH access) and the Fortinet catalogue's FNT-X-008 (identity compromise reaching VPN access).

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log + external identity event feed
data_sources.path: LC log, category=Audit; external SIEM-normalized identity events
data_sources.description: Privileged identity compromise indicator correlated with subsequent iDRAC authentication for the same identity.

detection_logic: Correlates an externally-sourced privileged-identity-compromise event (via a normalized lookup/index shared across catalogues) with a subsequent iDRAC login for the same identity within 60 minutes.
spl:
index=identity_events OR index=idrac
| eval stage=case(index="identity_events" AND event_type="privileged_identity_compromise","1_identity_compromised", index="idrac" AND sourcetype="idrac_audit" AND event="Login" AND result="Success","2_idrac_access", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=60m startswith=eval(stage="1_identity_compromised")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, host, src_ip, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a normalized cross-catalogue identity-event feed (e.g. from the Red Hat IPA or Fortinet FortiAuthenticator detections in this library, or any equivalent SIEM-correlated identity-compromise signal) — this is the most environment-specific detection in the iDRAC catalogue and needs real integration work before deployment.
investigation_steps: Confirm the identity-compromise finding from the source system.
Treat the iDRAC session as compromised and investigate per IDRAC-004's guidance.
response_guidance: Suspend the identity across all systems it has access to, not just iDRAC; disconnect any active iDRAC session.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: external privileged identity compromise -> iDRAC login, same identity

title: iDRAC Compromise Leads to Coordinated Logging Evasion
description: An administrator compromise (IDRAC-004) is followed by a syslog destination change (IDRAC-066) and/or SEL clear (IDRAC-070) within the same session — the iDRAC-specific version of the defense-evasion sequence pattern repeated across every catalogue in this library (Red Hat's auditd-stop-then-tamper pattern, Fortinet's FNT-X-010 fleet-wide control impairment).

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log
data_sources.description: Authentication compromise correlated with subsequent logging-tamper events.

detection_logic: Correlates a compromised-login pattern with a subsequent syslog-configuration change or SEL clear on the same device within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=idrac sourcetype=idrac_audit
| eval stage=case(event="Login" AND result="Success","1_login", event="ConfigChange" AND cfgattr IN ("SyslogEnable","SyslogServer"),"2_logging_evasion", event="SELCleared","2_logging_evasion", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference with IDRAC-002 to require the login itself be preceded by failures for the highest-confidence variant of this correlation.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Preserve any remaining external logs immediately.
response_guidance: Isolate the device from remote management, restore logging, and audit every action taken during the session.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: login -> syslog change or SEL clear, same device

title: Coordinated Destructive Attack: Privileged Login to Storage Deletion to Boot Failure
description: The named destructive attack chain from the specification: a privileged login, followed by storage deletion (IDRAC-080/081/083), followed by a power cycle, resulting in a boot failure — the complete data-destruction sequence available to an attacker with iDRAC access, executed entirely below the operating system where no host-level ransomware/EDR protection can intervene.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log
data_sources.description: Full timeline from authentication through storage destruction and subsequent reboot.

detection_logic: A three-stage transaction spanning login, storage-destructive action (virtual disk delete or secure erase), and reboot, for the same device within 20 minutes.
spl:
index=idrac
| eval stage=case(sourcetype="idrac_audit" AND event="Login" AND result="Success","1_login", sourcetype="idrac_storage" AND event IN ("VirtualDiskDeleted","SecureErase"),"2_storage_destroyed", sourcetype="idrac_audit" AND event="PowerControl" AND action IN ("Reset","PowerCycle"),"3_reboot", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=20m startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: No legitimate case for this exact sequence outside a fully-documented, deliberate decommissioning procedure — treat any unticketed occurrence as an active data-destruction emergency.
investigation_steps: Treat as the highest-priority incident this catalogue can raise.
Engage backup/recovery procedures immediately — this action is not reversible without one.
response_guidance: Suspend the acting account, notify executive/legal stakeholders given the likely business impact, and begin recovery from backup immediately.

title: iDRAC Console/Boot Activity Correlated With Hypervisor Administrative Change
description: On a hypervisor host, iDRAC Virtual Console access or a boot-configuration change (IDRAC-020/032) is followed by an administrative change on the hypervisor itself (e.g. an ESXi root-account or configuration event, correlatable with this library's own ESXi catalogue where deployed) — chaining out-of-band access to its most consequential possible outcome on a virtualization host: control over every guest VM it runs.

data_sources.name: iDRAC + hypervisor logs
data_sources.path: LC log; ESXi/Hyper-V administrative event log
data_sources.description: Console/boot activity correlated with subsequent hypervisor administrative changes for the same physical host.

detection_logic: Correlates an iDRAC console-session or boot-override event with a subsequent hypervisor-level administrative event (sourced from this library's ESXi catalogue or an equivalent Hyper-V feed) for the same physical host within 60 minutes.
spl:
index=idrac OR index=esxi
| eval stage=case(index="idrac" AND (event="VirtualConsoleSessionStart" OR event="BootOverride"),"1_oob_access", index="esxi" AND (eventtype="admin_login" OR eventtype="config_change"),"2_hypervisor_change", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=60m startswith=eval(stage="1_oob_access")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: Requires a physical-host-to-hypervisor-instance mapping and, ideally, this library's own ESXi threat detection catalogue deployed alongside it — a genuinely cross-catalogue correlation that needs real integration work.
investigation_steps: Confirm both events against change management.
If unconfirmed, treat the hypervisor and every guest VM it runs as potentially compromised.
response_guidance: Isolate the physical host and hypervisor management access; audit every guest VM for signs of tampering.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: iDRAC console/boot activity -> hypervisor administrative change, same physical host

title: OpenManage Enterprise Compromise Reaches Fleet-Wide iDRAC Impact
description: An OpenManage Enterprise administrator compromise (IDRAC-100) is followed by a fleet-wide firmware deployment (IDRAC-102) or remote command job (IDRAC-103) affecting multiple iDRACs — the Dell equivalent of the Fortinet catalogue's FNT-X-003 (FortiManager compromise reaching fleet-wide impact) and the direct realization of the risk OME's own architecture creates: one compromised console account controlling every managed server.

data_sources.name: OME audit log
data_sources.description: Full session timeline from compromised login through fleet-wide action.

detection_logic: A two-stage transaction: OME admin login-after-failures, followed by a fleet-wide firmware deployment or remote command job, within 60 minutes.
spl:
index=ome sourcetype=ome_audit OR index=ome sourcetype=ome_job
| eval stage=case(sourcetype="ome_audit" AND event="Login" AND result="Success","1_admin_compromised", sourcetype="ome_job" AND event IN ("FirmwareDeployment","JobExecuted") AND device_count>=5,"2_fleet_action", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction user maxspan=60m startswith=eval(stage="1_admin_compromised")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, user, src_ip, stage
tuning_guidance: Same identity-join and legitimate-deployment caveats as the FortiManager equivalent (FNT-X-003) — validate against your organization's normal OME administrator workflow before enabling as a paging alert.
investigation_steps: Treat as the highest-priority incident this catalogue can raise for OME.
Identify every affected device and halt further deployment immediately.
response_guidance: Suspend the OME account, halt all pending jobs, and prepare to roll back every affected device to its known-good state.

title: Post-Exploitation Fleet Reconnaissance Following Suspected iDRAC Vulnerability Exploitation
description: This detection does not claim to identify exploitation of a specific iDRAC CVE directly — as with the Fortinet catalogue's FNT-X-012, iDRAC telemetry frequently cannot observe an authentication-bypass or memory-corruption exploit primitive reaching the management interface via a crafted Redfish/HTTP request. Instead it looks for post-exploitation behaviors real iDRAC-targeting research and incident reports have described: unexplained administrative activity immediately followed by system inventory gathering and new local-account creation, without a preceding normal login pattern. Treat as a low-confidence hunting search, not a precision alert.

data_sources.name: iDRAC audit log
data_sources.description: Administrative activity and account-creation events without a corresponding expected authentication pattern.

detection_logic: Flags a system-inventory/discovery API call sequence immediately followed by local account creation, where the acting session does not match a known-good administrator baseline — a coarse behavioral proxy for post-exploitation activity, not a signature for any specific vulnerability.
spl:
index=idrac
| eval stage=case((sourcetype="idrac_redfish" AND api_uri="*/Systems/*" AND api_method="GET"),"1_recon", (sourcetype="idrac_audit" AND event="UserCreated"),"2_new_account", 1==1, null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction src_ip maxspan=15m startswith=eval(stage="1_recon")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| lookup idrac_source_baseline.csv src_ip OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, src_ip, host, user, stage
tuning_guidance: High false-positive potential given the coarse behavioral proxy — this is explicitly a hunting search for use during a declared Dell PSIRT advisory window affecting your deployed iDRAC firmware version, not a standing production alert. Do not claim this detects a specific CVE.
investigation_steps: Cross-reference the source IP against current Dell PSIRT advisories and your iDRAC firmware version.
Manually review the full activity sequence and any account created.
response_guidance: If a matching, currently-unpatched CVE exists for your firmware version, treat as a probable compromise: patch immediately and audit the account roster.
